reviews.text: Huge museum with a range of exhibits, from old to the most modern, as to be expected typical entrance, security set-up, with passport linked to your ticket (trip.com) fast and efficient, make sure your power bank is triple CCC certified, or you will probably have it taken off you, the same at all high value areas, aeroplanes, high speed railway etc. Mine is CCC. Bag lockers, drink machines, sit down toilets, and heaps of gift stores. Two steps past security exists you are not getting back in that way.... Tiananmen square is within the security zone, so get both of them ticked off your list of sites to see. Close to subway line 1 or line 2, hope you like stairs......

A must-go-to Museum, as it houses huge collections of cultural relics from beginning of China history to the later Qing dynasty. Extremely large and it took at least three hours to complete a single floor. The Museum is located opposite the Great Hall of People, which is also near to Tiananmen Square. Secure your timeslot a week before your intended visit through the Museum website and. Drop off at 贵实楼饭店 or Grand Hotel Beijing, and walk about 10 minutes to reach the security entry of the Museum.

Extremely large museum with huge complex and ridiculously large collection of artifacts you’ll never finish in one day. Other than the permanent exhibitions, there’s also some paid exhibitions such as the Respin Russian art exhibition. The basement one history of china permanent exhibition is the highlight. If you can, just visit this exhibition. Complex is huge, be prepared to walk a lot, children might not enjoy it, so I think kids above 12 years old is better. Bring some snacks as it’s very crowded and tiring. Everyone just rests at the steps and have some snacks. Exhibits are great but the toilets are not. So minus stars for the insufficiency of toilets plus strong urine smell in every toilet. That’s unacceptable for such a large government institution. Possibly toilets only make up for 1% of the building size. Very strange ratio since toilets are a basic human need. It’s also close to Tiananmen Square, you can enjoy museum until closing time then head across the road to Tiananmen square for the flag descending ceremony. But there’s always so many people, so you might see more heads and phones than anything.

Huge museum, we managed to only cover the main permanent exhibits. Remember to reserve your tickets on WeChat mini app ahead of time. If you didn’t manage to do so, just book a VIP tour on trip.com (at extra cost!) with guide. This can be done even the day before but doesn’t come cheap. Admission to museum also includes admission to Tiananmen Square (which usually requires separate reservation)! Enjoy!

There's just too much to see here in this museum, in a good way. Unfortunate for me, many things were in Chinese. Of course, a short description might be available, but the actual juicy details would have been better if these had been available in English as well. What I furthermore disliked was the way in which communism was portrayed positively (as expected) and how other things were (such as poverty) not shown. However, as for cultural aspects, such as food and traditional Chinese medicine, there are so many maquettes, which are really fun to look at. It wasn't crowded at all, and even if it were, the space is huge. Beautiful building (on the inside). Be forewarned that it is quite a distance walking to it. It's better to take the subway by the way, because taxis aren't allowed to stop near it. Also, the coffee is really expensive there, but that taste is good.

To visit any government museums and other points of interest, you need to download WeChat and most of the institutions have something called mini programs in WeChat where you can check the activities and buy ticket We got lucky and came to know tickets are available 7 days in advance around 5 PM every day so be ready to book It is opposite the Tiananmen Square and be prepared to stand in line for the visit as they check tickets and for foreigners visitors you need to carry a passport Musuem has good layout and to understand the rich history of China be prepared to spend 2 to 3 hours in Musuem Lot of Buddhist artifacts are placed in top floor and calligraphy details are showcased to describe how it’s important to Chinese culture It can get busy so plan ahead and the Musuem is well maintained In most places I did find English translation or use Audio guide along with phone translator

Huge and wide-ranging museum, front ancient history to modern technologies and even some CCP artifacts. Book tickets on the website or WeChat 7 days before at 8pm Beijing time exactly. Tickets book out in minutes. Enter at the north side of the museum, DO NOT enter Tiananmen square security as it's a separate entrance. You'll exit the museum directly into Tiananmen square, so see that (or the forbidden City) after your museum visit. There's a few vending machines and cafes inside, the one in the basement is the cheapest. There's also filtered water dispensers for bottles only. I spent 6 hours here, could have spent much more!

Must go if you... - want to know the history of different Chinese dynasty - understand the Chinese civilization and culture better - into archaeology, history, arts and ancient times - know the development of modern China Do not go if you... - love to complain about walking too much - hate crowded places - do not have time to spare

National Museum of China (中国国家博物馆) A China SIM card is required to book a visiting slot. On-site booking is not available. Advance reservations can be made 1–7 days in advance & admission is free. Online booking opens daily from 5:00 PM. The museum is closed on Mondays. Bring passport for ID verification when collecting tickets.

You'll need to reserve tickets via their official website or via trip.com. foc. Tickets open 7 days before the day of visit. At around 5pm. There are security checks so add about 15mins for that. Head to B1 for the history of china. The exit is in the middle of level 1.

The National Museum of China is an absolute MUST for any Beijing itinerary. Be aware: **you MUST book tickets online in advance** (book as early as possible!). To truly appreciate the sheer scale and priceless treasures inside, **arrive as early as possible when it opens**. You'll avoid the massive crowds and have a much more peaceful, enjoyable experience exploring China's most significant cultural relics, spanning thousands of years. Highly recommended for visitors from all over the world!
Has a bunch of special exhibitions but the main focus is the one below ground level which has priceless artifacts from prehistoric times to the Qing Dynasty.

If you like history, this is probably one of the best museums to visit in Beijing. The admission is free but you have to reserve tickets through a mini app on WeChat. It could be difficult to get tickets. They release new tickets every day at 5 pm. The best one was the Ancient China exhibition, but the line could also get extremely long. You’d better visit it either in the morning or late before their closing time. There were also plenty of temporary exhibitions. You could expect to spend at least 3 hours here.

A pretty big museum show casing much of Chinese ancient and recent history. However I felt that it was a little lackluster in terms of interesting things. Good news is once you exit here you can check out the tiananmen plaza so you don’t need to come a second time to visit the plaza.

Before planing my visit, a friend warned me this spot is popular with tourists, so I came with my low expectation… and honestly, it still felt overwhelming. The moment I got off the train, it was chaos—long queues, security checks (three times, from train to the entrance), and some seriously impatient staff. Not the chill experience I hoped for. 🤯 If you’re planning to come, pack your patience and maybe a podcast for the wait. 🤞🏻Good luck!

To access the museum, you need to make reservation via their website or WeChat mini app first at least 7 days in advance and admission is free. The museum is quite huge and separated into 2 wings and many floors. You should check out the floor plan first and decide which part you would be interested in. The most popular section seems to be the Ancient China which you have to queue to get in. There are both temporary and permanent exhibitions with lots of invaluable items and historical content to check out (with some English explanation). After your visit, you can proceed to other nearby attractions in the same area.

Went there on 14 Nov, appointment is needed, you can do via WeChat, very convenient in China. This museum is super huge comparing to the very few museums I went to. You can easily spend half a day there. I was in rush, if I have the chance to revisit Beijing, I would definitely go back to learn more about the arts, history and culture. 🫶🏻🇨🇳

It is very hard, almost impossible to buy tickets. It opens 7 days in advance I think and need to be really fast. We had help from our colleagues. Very nice, learned a lot about history, technology, art. I would visit again next time when I visit Beijing, if I get lucky to buy ticket again.

It's free to enter but you have to book a slot in advance as they control the number of visitors per time slot. This is a huge museum and after visiting, I can understand why there are so many locals, because there's really alot to see, even in the permanent exhibits halls that it's impossible to finish in a day if you are going to view them in detail. We did just the 古代中国 hall, focusing only on the more interesting key exhibits and it already took us 2 hrs.

Unless you are a history geek, I don't highly recommend coming here. The lines can get extremely long and not too many activities besides reading about history. Security is also very tight. You need to drink any drinks you have in front of the security staff and you cannot take out any selfie sticks. Thankfully staff were still kind
Amazing museum. They even had a robot dog to carry people heavy items that needed to be checked. Very cool up close. What a history the main Hall with paintings were very moving.

Enormous museum with more than just the culture an history of China. For most foreigners the basement is the most interesting floor to visit which displays the history from 20.000 years ago till recent.

Free entry but you need a ticket to enter! There is a crowd to enter the museum.. took us 20 mins to enter after all the bag and human checks. Main attraction is in the basement which tells you the history of China. The place is horribly big so be prepared to walk and walk!
Entry is free for tourists; however, you need to prebook a visit time slot one week in advance via the WeChat app. Many Chinese historical relics are on display, and the exhibits are exquisite.

FABULOUS MUSEUM AND ANOTHER MUST VISIT.....HOWEVER !!!! I strongly recommend to everyone to get a phone translator, as when I was present there, there were sections where only the Chinese language was used and I could prehaps see the beautiful exposition, however I couldn't get any meaningful informations. It is rather large, so you could easily spend half a day there, or even a full day if you are heavily into China history. I give 4 stars instead of 5, because getting tickets was rather confusing and if I recall well, they took our passports and gave them later back with free tickets (I have no clue if Chinese pay, or foreigners, we just got it back and that was that), not to mention that Chinese que's are not very well organized, so it was rather messy. Apart from getting the tickets and some sections being solely in Chinese, it was rather enjoyable. Located in absolute center it's once again a must.

An extremely popular museum and you need to book a ticket before entering. For anything popular in Beijing I would book at least a week in advance. We found places were booked out 3 days in advance even during quieter times.

An absolutely massive museum with five exhibition floors, one of which is underground. Admission is free, except for the ticketed exhibitions. Extremely scarce reservation tickets available for foreigners, usually requiring you to compete to claim one at least a week ahead of the actual visit date. It's easier to fetch a reservation if you are a Chinese national or purchase a ticketed exhibition admission (both of which are not easily accessible). This is easily one of the hardest places to gain access to in Beijing, and requires you to revolve your entire travel plans around it if you are interested in visiting it but have a limited stay duration. You cannot simply show up with your passport. Expect to spend at least 4-5 hours in here, or else you will find yourself rushing to see everything. The bulk of the content is on the fourth and B1 underground floors. I would rate this a 5/5, but the insane difficulty in securing a reservation ticket and need for you to adjust your travel plans strictly for it is simply ridiculous.

It's a good museum and not too overwhelming, despite the awe-inspiring size of the place. It's very airy and the exhibits are limited and tightly focused. It's got a good mix of various things, although each individual exhibit isn't really tied to any of the others through any thematic link. I enjoyed the jade exhibit and the wood-carving exhibit, and some of the ceramics were most impressive. The staff speaks a decent amount of English, but be warned, you're going to need your passport to get in.
The closest way to get there is the subway line1 Tian-anmen east exit C/D. If you walk from another direction, it will be far and there will be many passport check points.

‘A must visit to better understand China’ I visited the national museum to better understand China through history. The place is immense and offers many exhibitions. I specifically enjoyed the history exhibitions. Be mindful to book your tickets in advance. I got lucky there was still availability for the same day! One thing that struck me was that the staff was walking around with signs for crowd control such as ‘dont scream’ ‘don’t play rough’.

Visited in November 2023. Fantastic journey into history - as expected from a top 3 museum in China - the quantity and quality of exhibits transports one back in time. Mandatory to reserve in advance though it’s free. Booked tickets via WeChat app mini program. Be patient - if it doesn’t work / go through first time, try again (as with many China based apps - persistence pays off). Security checks to enter premises are efficient. All national Monuments close on Monday so plan around this.

Book via wechat 7 days in advance otherwise you won't get tickets at all, this place is very popular with the locals too. Recommend to start from the exhibition at the basement, where they exhibit in accordance with the history/dynasty line of China. Incredible bronze and other artfacts items from more than 3000years ago are just presented right in front of your eyes... I m total overwhelmed... better to search for information of items that you might interested to witness before hand otherwise you might be bombarded with artifacts while lost in information/translation. There is a dining area on the basement floor, but possibly due to exihibition-safty concern only cold/dry food (like cold noodles in sesame sauce) was offered, so maybe you can pack your own sandwiches or snacks to eat inside canteen area. Visiting time for us was 4-5hours FYI.

A huge sprawling museum with loads or Chinese and international artifacts. It's a modern and spacious layout with loads to see, you'll want to get there early in the day to be able to enjoy the all exhibits at a relaxed pace. The museum is free but you will need to book tickets via WeChat, as entries are managed to prevent overcrowding. Make sure to bring some water if it's hot, as the queues can be quite loong even with a timeslot booked. For tourists like myself, have your passport handy as you'll need it for ID when getting in, also note that upon entry everyone gets a quick bag search and scan for security.

Biggest museum I ever been. There's so much to see and a few hours is definitely not enough to see all of it. You have to do booking in WeChat to visit this museum. This museum is strict with the security, no selfie stick is allowed. Kindly view the rules and regulations before entering the museum.

We went here in Feb 2016, It was really interesting when you got into the museum. once you have got past all the security checks and queues. when you get into the part to purchase your tickets, if your a visitor GO RIGHT, if you go opposite, you will experience a fate worst than hell. It is a free for all and no sense of what queueing is, it is utter bedlam. You can purchase food in the museum and drinks, you can also purchase gifts at the gift shop, you can probably buy them cheaper outside, but the quality is better in the museum. If this review was helpful, please like.

Huge museum, and very crowded. We queued for about 30 minutes in a very unruly line before being able to enter. You have to have your passport, as with everything in China, and the museum entry is free. No maps are available in English, and not all exhibitions have English descriptions. The basement (B1) has the Ancient China exhibition - very informative, with a lot of artifacts. We liked the room where they display presents from other governments to the Chinese government which was on the fourth floor.
I loved this museum, it is very big over many floors. It has a wide range of historical items. A must see. Do not take a bit backpack and make sure you take your passport. A must visit museum.
Very impressive place to learn a lot about Chinese history. The museum covers many different areas of Chinese culture. You can spend many hours in there.

Free, large museum. Avoid going on weekends and holidays to avoid the crowds. Opens at 9am closed on Mondays. Some exhibits offer English translations while others do not. A lot of various art exhibits with historical context.

Good place to learn the ancient history of China (not so balanced if you are interested in modern history). Great exhibits. Foreigners can gain entry with passport. 100% free to enter. Place is huge, a bit overwhelmed.
1. Lots of exhibits 2. Decent temperature inside 3. Clean bathrooms 4. Free entry with passport 5. Some snacks and drinks available inside (nothing fancy)
A carnival of relics and arts. If you want to explore Chinese culture a little bit just in one day, this is where you should go. Remember to bring your ID, and the admission fee is ZERO.

There are ancient Chinese cultural relics of various periods. There are also Roman Empire commodities traded through the Silk Road.There are also some neighboring countries Unlike the British Museum, there are no cultural relics looted or stolen from other countries.

You can visit this area consisting of Tiananmen Square, Monument of People’s Great Heroes, and National Museum of China by using the underpass. Just taking a photo behind this building is already satisfying. It really looks alike with Great Hall of People, cant tell the difference unless the symbol on its top
Great variety of Chinese history, make sure you book a time slot, lots of security procedures, gifts are fun to get from here
very cool and big place with a lot of people. a bunzh of historical artefacts. buy tickets in advance or u cannot go here

I'm a little bit disappointed because this musuem don't have what I looking for. l like map, infographic, good atmosphere but there only have sculpture and description. You have to have enough time to see everything. And must important I'm not sure that is real or not. 😭

The exhibition on Ancient China was excellent. I learned a lot about the history of this country. It goes from Paleolithic (10000 BC) until 20th century. All the signs are translated in English as well. When done, I was too tired to see something else but my visit was worth it. Also, from the museum you can exit to Tianmen square so you don't need to go again through security.
First,it's free, but you need to make a reservation, I used Wechat. It's very big, I didn't see everything.

Free entrance but you must get the tickets showing passport before entering to the left and right of museum entrance. Start at the 4th floor where various types of presidential gifts and artifacts are displayed. Tons of brass budda statues abd porcelain on other floors.

Free entrance for foreigner. Cannot bring selfie stick. Security very tight. Close on Monday, daily open till 4.30pm. Place very huge with 3 levels and an underground level. There is plenty of stalls selling souvenir and a cafe and convenient stalls that sell drinks and snacks. Need to come early as need to go through security check to enter Tiananmen square first which has long queue during major festive season or weekend. The museum is located just in from of Tiananmen Gate behind the Chairman Mao mouseleum.
Awesome place … Must online register for visit. You can only go in at the time u reserve.

I suggest a visit here before going out anywhere else in Beijing. Going here first helps understand China's rich history. Plan at least 3 hours (unless you want to go to the special exhibits too which are quite interesting as well). Take anything modern with a grain of salt but the museum is well made obviously. Also you are now in the heart of the city and as such close to many other things. Be wary, the wait may be very long to enter, up to an hour.
You need to spend at least two days in order to tour the whole museum. There are themed exhibitions which are worth to visit.
Located close to the Tiananmen square, this is a huge museum with a significant collection of exhibits. Make sure you carry some ID with you to get an entry ticket which is free.

Amazing pieces of history. Great lighting and layout. However it’s just too popular amongst tour groups with pushing a few people pushing around to get up close to snap photos. Overall a good place to visit if you’re patient.

Worth the waiting to get through security. As the museum is in same area as Tiennamen Square and The Forbidden Palace, it may be worth going on week days rather than the weekend. A huge place with so much history to explore. Took me about 5 hours to slowly and carefully explore level 1 and level 2. Signage was mostly in both Chinese and English. They had run out of museum maps and audio tours when I arrived so had to make do with display signage. Not many places to sit while working through the displays. Being a little older I did find that a real issue. Unfortunately I didn't get to level 3. Well worth the effort to have a good long look 😊

A massive (5 floors), impressive looking museum filled with interesting historical artefacts. However, they did make it seem like China was the inventor of all the good things we have in the world! Wasn't able to see everything because I just got too tired.
Gigantic place, i had to rush through most of it because it took too long. Was in there about 3h
Its definately a must visit if you are into history of China.The museum is very big...it took me 5hrs just to complete 1 floor.Do remember to do your reservation prior visit.
Great experience. Beautiful paintings and artifacts. Museum is free just remember to BRING PASSPORT!

the security is so over the top. not enough info, pointers, booklets available for people to guide them around in the huge museum. nor on the outside, for that matter. we started from the bottom floors and immediately got bored. we had no idea what collections other floors had -- couldnt see a floor map index -- so we left.

Entry is strictly by reservation via its official website which may be a bit inconvenient for tourists. Try to book it days in advance. You may also try third party platform such as Trip.com. Museum is too huge to visit all levels in a day. If you only have a day to spend there, visit the hall on Chinese history at the basement.

Vast museum featuring artifacts spanning literally millennia of history and prehistory. I think they can sell out of tickets on busy days (or if not, then you could still be stuck in a very long line), so call ahead if you can.

It's a good museum and not too overwhelming, despite the awe-inspiring size of the place. It's very airy and the exhibits are limited and tightly focused. It's got a good mix of various things, although each individual exhibit isn't really tied to any of the others through any thematic link. I enjoyed the jade exhibit and the wood-carving exhibit, and some of the ceramics were most impressive. The staff speaks a decent amount of English, but be warned, you're going to need your passport to get in.
It's free BUT You need to book online at least 7 days in advance. If u can't do it, maybe your hotel concierge can help. We arrived, no booking, no entry, no exceptions.

Foreigner, forget it! Unless you are a fan of quests, you won’t (or won’t want to waste your time and goodwill on) get through the maze of the access booking system. It’s like you are trying to get to a top-secret facility, rather than the National Museum. In some of trip reports I read that this museum “is not that popular with foreign tourists”. Well, now I see that this is not without reason!

It is huge!!! And its free. You can book your tickets within 3 days ahead if it happens there is a Famous exhibition. Really like the Ancient Chinese Exhibition in the basement. It is always there. Will give you a brief introduction of.Chinese Culture and history. Has a very good collection and many Famous artifact.

tourist, donno chinese... no wechat of couse. roads are blocked around the park and the square, you have to walk a lot. the line is long. we were rejected the enterence and told i have to ask a chinse friends to make an reservation via wechat. they showed that through their smartphone translation app. dont waste time, and ask your chinese friends to book it!

Massive museum with a wide variety of exhibits of art and history. Free for tourists from other countries when you present your passport. The Ancient China permanent exhibit is reason enough to come if you like learning about history, as it takes you from the beginnings of civilization to the end of the Qing dynasty in a well put together exhibit. The other exhibits are interesting and change regularly. They have cafes and gift shops enough to satisfy any need while visiting. Definitely add this to your list when visiting Beijing.

AMAZING PLACE. Lots of artifacts ranging from golden buddhas to bronze vessels (LOTS OF THEM.) fill the museum. There's so much that you won't be able to finish it in one day! The museum is also relatively clean, and has a modern design. Entry is free at this museum. The gift shop is also small, but cozy and nice! They sell many accessories for reasonable prices. I would recommend this place to anyone who goes to Beijing!

Nice museum. Excellent exhibition of ancient chinese culture. Entry is free, only passport verification for the tourists done. However it is always crowded. So must have some time in hand and the waiting is worth really.
Very large place, but they have limited time for every appointment, very organized. The only down side is you need to walk almost 1 km before entering.

National Museum of China flanks the eastern side of Tiananmen Square in Beijing, China. The museum's mission is to educate about the arts and history of China. It is directed by the Ministry of Culture of the People's Republic of China. I've been to several museums in my lifetime and I can easily say this is one of the largest museums I've ever seen. Bring your passport and go to the customer service desk. The museum offers discounts entry for international visitors.

I highly recommend this museum, if you have a couple of days or more to spend in Forbidden City and the square! Plan for at least 4 hours for the museum (free admission) and remember to take your passport with you. There is so much to see and so many incredible collections and artifacts to view! Don't skip it!

Beijing has lot of places to visit. A museum portrays the glorious past of its nation. I visited he national museum of china once. The each and every detail are preserved here. You can visualize the chinese past while visiting this museum. If you want to learn about the past culture and its traditions, this is the best place in Beijing. Hopefully, you are going to love this place.

a Huge museum to have a trip, it took me 3 days, about 9 hours to finish all the part that I love. It may take more time if you want to finish all the show rooms in the museum. One more thing, the ticket room of museum is closed from 15:30, which means you can't get in after that time, and is closed at 17:00, business days from Tuesday to Sunday.

I made the mistake of going on a Saturday at 9am. I must have been in line (really more of a mosh pit) with nearly 30,000 people (no joke). It was super hot and elbows were sharp. As a westerner it was very unruly and uncomfortable. However, the exhibit on ancient China was worth the tussle and hassle. Fortunately, the museum is huge and therefore the crowds somehow fit.

Superb museum with splendid collections! I went there with my friend during the Chinese Spring Festival period, and there was the temporary art exhibition of Meilin Han, the designer of Beijing 2008 signs. And huge amount of paintings as well as sculptures of rooster (because of 2017 is the year of Rooster according to Chinese culture). There were also this Chinese Calligraphy session that impressed us very much. The best thing about the museum is that you can expect almost every piece of their collections has an introduction in English. We arrived in the afternoon, so it was only 3 hours to spend (yet it was really an amazing tour). Will definitely go again to continue enjoying the ancient China exhibitions in the basement.

I am sure this an excellent Museum but one should note that you need to book tickets 3 days in advance, yes you can get some on the day but you should book in advance as they sell out quickly. If you go with a tour guide make sure you have done your research first as you cannot always trust what you are being told.
Very nice and grand museum .... no entry fees too ... nearby to tiananmen sqaure ... recommend

Dont go on Saturday it is packed. It's closed on Monday's! I was very impressed by the sheer size of this museum 2.2 million square feet. I spent approximately 20 hours over the course of a week. The bottom floor was ancient China. Truly outstanding. The Song Dynasty exhibit was remarkable.Don't go on Saturday. I was lucky to be able to see the Chinese master woodcarver exhibition while here. Woodcarving master Lu Guangzheng's artwork "The way to the sun." Lu's exhibition is a showcase of traditional woodcarving techniques unique to the city of Dongyang, in East China's Zhejiang province. Inspired by the ancient Silk Road, Lu's "One Belt and Road" exhibition can be divided into three categories. I would hate to dust these amazing woodworking pieces.
Best place to learn about Chinese history and culture, as well as exhibits about the achievements made by China in modern history.

an amazing place, security outside was really lovely especially me being so confused looking like a proper tourist. one of the few major tourist attractions they accepted i can speak both chinese and english (completely mad i know) but is filled with an enormous amount of rich history about china great for an all day event as my chinese cousin had to rush home to fetch her chinese ID card in addition to having separate lines with nationals and foreigners only took a sec for me and my partner (the foreign nationals) to go through security the security guard shouted at me on accident and pushed me quite hard when telling me to turn around but quickly apologised which was nice haha but having to wait for my 90 yr old chinese grandad in the chinese nationals security line took ages for him to come through as they gave him a full security check which i thought was a bit strange.it is truly a lovely museum next only had 2 hours to spend and was only able to go through half of the underground portion cos of our little hiccup. will deffo be back next time fully prepared. would suggest if want to visit to clear a full day for this and make sure everyone has their passport or chinese ID card on them as they would not accept my cousins driving license or my grandad's alternate senior ID. highly recommend to anyone visiting beijing whether they are on a excursion or live in the country.

First rate exhibits of historical artefacts across a the broad swath of it's history presented in a cogent manner and context. Provision of WiFi for guests is a major plus as is the fairly comprehensive availability of english translation on most exhibit cards. Do note that foreign nationals require pre-registration through the museum's website for the limited number of tickets available daily. I recommend booking your reservation as soon as the window opens (approximately two weeks ahead) as on many days all two thousand foreign national tickets are taken days in advance.

The National Museum of China is located at the east side of Tiananmen Square which was formerly called the Museum of Chinese History and Museum of Chinese Revolution. It is 313 meters long, 149 meters wide and 40 meters high, covering an area of 69,000 square meters. The building was one of the “Ten Great Constructions” completed for the 10th Anniversary of the People’s Republic of China in 1959. After four years’ renovation and expansion, the new National Museum reopened on Apr. 1st, 2011 which is the largest museum in the world. There are altogether 48 exhibition rooms in the new National Museum, ranging from 700-2000 square meters. The rooms of Ancient China and Road to Rejuvenation are the main basic exhibitions. There are nearly 3,000 historic relics from Yuanmou Man (1,700,000 years ago) to the abdication of the Qing Emperor in 1912 on display in ten exhibition halls. The modern and contemporary revolutionary relics since the First Opium War in 1840 to the founding of the People’s Republic of China in 1949 are also displayed in nine exhibition halls. There are also a variety of thematic exhibitions in the National Museum, such as the Arts of bronze, porcelain, jade, Chinese calligraphy and paintings, Buddhist statues, Ming and Qing furniture and coins etc.

really huge and educational museum - as it's the NATIONAL one. some temporary/special exhibitions are worth paying for watching. but people with slippers are not allowed to go in (i was turned down once) 別穿拖鞋去！
Huge museum which gives justice to the long history of China. You can follow it from the oldest beginnings to the first Chinese in space and today. Beautiful souvenirs in shops on each floor

This museum on Tiananmen Square measures 2.07 million square feet—surpassing New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art’s 2 million square feet—and reopened in 2011 after a decade-long renovation. It presents 5,000 years of Chinese history, as approved by the Ministry of Culture. (In other words, don’t expect much on the Great Leap Forward.) Artifacts include ancient Chinese Buddhist sculptures, a cowboy hat Deng Xiaoping wore on a visit to the U.S., and glazed pottery from the Tang dynasty. The museum also hosts temporary shows on subjects ranging from Leo Tolstoy to African art.

Le musée national se trouve sur la place Tiananmen. L'entrée est gratuite mais nous vous recommandons de réserver votre créneau d'entrée. Il faut prévoir également de passer un important dispositif de sécurité non seulement pour accéder à la zone où se trouve le musée et le musée en lui-même. En effet, une fois que vous sortirez du musée, vous arriverez directement sur la place Tiananmen, donc le contrôle se fait largement en amont. Comme pour tous les sites touristiques de Chine, c'est votre passeport qui fait office de billet d'entrée. Nous y sommes allés un après-midi et, après avoir passé pas mal de temps à faire la queue pour le contrôle, au moins 1h en tout, nous avons pu avoir accès au musée. Le bâtiment est immense et les collections sont réparties sur plusieurs niveaux. Il y avait énormément de monde quand nous y sommes allés, un dimanche après-midi. La foule était telle que l'accès à certaines galeries (notamment celle dédiée à la civilisation chinoise) était restreint et régulé par un système de file d'attente. Les objets exposés sont magnifiques et vraiment sublimes. Nous avons pu voir beaucoup de choses qu'il est rare de voir dans les musées, des pièces en cuivre, en bronze, des pierres, des joyaux, la couronne d'une des impératrices, etc. Malheureusement tout n'est pas toujours bien mis en valeur, et la foule compacte peut rendre la visite difficile. Il faut compter entre 2 et 3 heures de visite si vous voulez tout voir. Dommage qu'il y ait autant de monde et que les gens collent leurs doigts sur les vitrines...

中國國家博物館（National Museum of China），簡稱國博，位於北京市中心天安門廣場東側，東長安街南側，與人民大會堂東西相對稱，是代表國家收藏、研究、展示、闡釋中華文化代表性物證的最高歷史文化藝術殿堂​​，負有留存民族集體記憶、傳承國家文化基因、促進文明交流互鑑的重要使命，也是國家文化客廳。 中國國家博物館的前身可追溯至民國元年（1912年）成立的國立歷史博物館籌備處；2003年，中國歷史博物館和中國革命博物館合併組成中國國家博物館；2012年，中國國家博物館改擴建完成並正式對外開放。新館建築保留了原有老建築西、北、南建築立面，總用地面積7萬平方米，建築高度42.5米，地上5層，地下2層，展廳48個，建築面積近20萬平方米，是全世界單體建築面積最大的博物館。中國國家博物館有收藏數量143萬餘件，涵蓋古代文物、近現當代文物、藝術品等多種門類，涉及甲骨、青銅器、瓷器、玉器、金銀器、錢幣、佛造像、古籍善本、碑帖拓本、墓誌、璽印、書畫、雕塑、漆木家具、磚瓦石刻、琺瑯器、玻璃器、絲織品、工藝品、老照片、國家文物、民俗文物、革命文物等。

這館一走進去就兩個字：大、氣。 建築本體氣勢磅礴，天花板高到懷疑是不是能飛無人機，走廊寬得能打籃球，整體空間直接讓人感受到「國家級博物館就是不一樣」。 🖼️ 展品超多，看不完的歷史輸出 從史前時代到近代中國，從玉器青銅到近代文物，再到各種主題特展、臨時展，內容爆炸豐富。每個展廳都像一門歷史課＋社會課＋藝術課。 但跟團的時間永遠不夠用，導遊說「這只是走馬看花」，結果真的只能「眼睛掃過就走」。 🆕 館內設備真的新、動線也不錯 多媒體互動蠻多的，觸控螢幕、投影牆、語音導覽一應俱全。展板設計得清楚不囉唆（當然有些政治味還是蠻濃的，畢竟國家博物館嘛）。 📸 拍照可以但要收斂 雖然大部分展區都能拍照，但閃光燈絕對禁止。還有就是人很多，你拍展品的同時，別人可能也在拍你拍展品，懂的都懂。 👟 真的、非常、超級大館 走一圈下來，腳真的會懷疑人生。光是一個主展廳就能讓你走半天，根本就是「文化版體能測驗」。如果想細看每個展，建議自己來逛個一整天＋分段攻略，跟團真的只是開胃菜。 🍵 周邊休息區不多，建議自帶水＆快速能量補給品（小心別在展廳吃） 紀念品店很官方、很乾淨，但價格也很「首都價」，買起來請斟酌。

走進國博，彷彿穿越了時空的長廊，每一件展品都是一段歷史的縮影，每一幅壁畫都是一個時代的印記。從古代的陶器到近代的文獻，從精緻的玉器到雄渾的青銅器，國博的收藏涵蓋了中華文明的方方面面，展現了中華民族的智慧與創造力。 特別值得一提的是「古代中國」基本上陳列，它以朝代更迭為線索，系統地展示了中華文明的發展歷程。在這裡，可以看到商周的青銅器、漢代的玉器、唐宋的書畫，每一件都是國之瑰寶，讓人嘆為觀止。而「復興之路」展覽則展示了近現代中國的歷史變遷，讓人感受到民族復興的波瀾壯闊。國博不僅在展覽內容上做到了極致，其建築設計也同樣令人印象深刻。新館的現代化建築風格與老館的傳統元素結合，既展現了歷史的厚重感，也體現了時代的創新精神。 館內的佈局合理，導覽系統清晰，為參觀者提供了良好的觀展體驗。總之，中國國家博物館以其獨特的魅力和深遠的影響力，成為了傳播中華文化、促進文化交流的重要平台，值得每位熱愛文化的人前來參觀體驗。

中国国家博物馆（National Museum of China）简称国博，位于北京市中心天安门广场东侧，东长安街南侧，与人民大会堂东西相对称，是历史与艺术并重，集收藏、展览、研究、考古、公共教育、文化交流于一体的综合性博物馆。隶属于中华人民共和国文化部。中国国家博物馆是世界上建筑面积最大的博物馆，总建筑面积近20万平方米。总用地面积7万平方米。建筑高度42.5米，地上5层，地下2层... 建筑由两轴两区构成。两轴为：由西门到东门的东西轴线和由南到北的南北轴线。两区为：由中轴内中央大厅分隔的南北两个展区。西门面向天安门广场，与人民大会堂相对；北门面向长安街。南北艺术长廊长260米，高28米；顶部有368个采用中国传统建筑风格的藻井，有着独特的装饰、采光、照明和通风等作用。楼顶有近2万平方米的屋顶绿地，表现出了环保和节能的理念。

Története 1912-ig vezethető vissza, amikor megalakult az Országos Történeti Múzeum Előkészítő Iroda. A Tienanmen tértől keletre álló épület 1959-63 között épült, a Kínai Népköztársaság megalapításának tíz éves évfordulójára. 2003-ban a két különálló, de ugyanabban az épületben lévő múzeumokat összevonták (az északi szárnyban található Kínai Forradalom Múzeum és a déli szárnyban lévő Kínai Történeti Nemzeti Múzeum). Az ország legnagyobb művészeti múzeuma lett. Több mint 1,4 milliós gyűjteménnyel rendelkezik. A Múzeum felújítása és bővítése 2007-ben kezdődött, és 2011 márciusában fejeződött be, amikor a Múzeum újra megnyílt a nagyközönség előtt. Az új épület megtartotta a régi épület nyugati, északi és déli homlokzatát. A 70000 négyzetméternyi területet lefedő új épület 42,5 méter magas, a föld felett öt emeletből és a föld alatt két emeletből áll. Az összesen 48 galériával felújított múzeum közel 200 ezer m2 alapterületű. A bejáratnál tíz négyzet alakú oszlop látható. Alapterületét tekintve a világ legnagyobb egyépületes múzeuma. Bár Kína művészeti örökségének nagy része 1949 után Tajvanra került, a Kínai Nemzeti Múzeum állandó galériáiban több mint 600 000 kiállítás található. A múzeum eklektikus gyűjteményében megtalálhatók a neolitikus korszakból származó kerámiák, jáde alkotások, értékes Ming-vázák, kalligráfiák, festmények, antik szobrok és bronz boros edények, valamint Yuanmo ember és Pekingi ember megkövesedett maradványai. A Viaszgalériájában Mao, Konfuciusz és Marx viaszfigurái, valamint olyan modernebb ikonok is láthatók, mint David Beckham, Michael Jordan, vagy Marilyn Monroe.
